content.question: In Episode 2 the instructor described an Activity with a book analogy — which description best matches an Android Activity?

options.text: A single focused screen (a page in the app) that the user interacts with
A background service running without UI
A database used to store UI layouts
An XML-only resource with no code

content.explanation: An Activity represents a single screen with a user interface and handles user interaction, like a page in a book.
hints: Think of a screen or page

content.question: When creating a new Activity in Android Studio, the instructor pointed out a checkbox 'Generate layout file' — what does enabling that option do?

options.text: Creates the XML layout file alongside the Kotlin/Java activity file
Generates only unit tests for the activity

content.explanation: Toggling 'Generate layout file' produces both the activity controller file and an associated activity_*.xml UI file.
hints: Unchecking it creates only the Kotlin/Java file
The layout name appears as ActivityMyAndroid

content.question: The instructor explained the 'source language' dropdown when creating an activity — what effect does choosing Kotlin or Java have?

options.text: It determines whether the generated controller file is .kt (Kotlin) or .java (Java)
It converts all XML to a language-specific format
It enforces Kotlin-only libraries at build time
It changes the AndroidManifest package name

content.explanation: Choosing the source language controls which controller file type is generated; the UI XML is separate.
hints: You can select either language for the activity controller

content.question: According to Episode 2, how do you declare an id for a view in XML so it can be referenced later?
content.explanation: Use android:id='@+id/name' to declare and create the id resource; later references can use @id/name.

content.question: To access a button declared in XML from Kotlin, which approach did the instructor demonstrate?

options.text: Declare a variable and assign it using findViewById(R.id.your_id)
Import the XML file into Kotlin directly
Use the XML id string directly without lookup
No code is needed — XML and Kotlin are automatically linked by name

content.explanation: He showed introducing the component into Kotlin by creating a variable and assigning it with findViewById using the generated R.id identifier.
hints: The pattern is val btn: Button = findViewById(R.id.login_button)
You must import the Button class

content.question: The instructor changed an XML id and then saw an error in Kotlin — what must be kept consistent to avoid that error?

options.text: The id used in XML and the id referenced in Kotlin (R.id.name) must match
The Kotlin variable name must equal the XML file name
The layout file must be named exactly like the activity class
The app package must change when id changes

content.explanation: If you rename the id in XML, you must update the code that references R.id.<that_name> to match the new id, otherwise findViewById will fail to resolve.
hints: Keep XML id and code reference in sync

content.question: What file extension indicates a Kotlin source file in Android Studio?
content.explanation: Kotlin source files use the .kt extension.

content.question: Which extension indicates a Java source file?
content.explanation: Java source files use the .java extension.

content.question: If you uncheck 'Generate layout file' when creating an activity, what do you get?

options.text: Only the Kotlin/Java activity file is created
Only the XML layout is created
A service file is created instead

content.explanation: Unchecking that option means only the controller file is generated; the layout file is omitted.
hints: You can create the layout later manually

content.question: What UI mode did the instructor switch to when editing the drawable to preview changes?
content.explanation: He used split view so the shape XML and the design preview are visible concurrently.
hints: Split view shows both design and XML

content.question: Where do you typically declare color resource names used across layouts?
content.explanation: Color resources are defined in res/values/colors.xml and referenced by name in layouts.

content.question: Which XML attribute syntax declares and creates an id resource?
content.explanation: Use @+id/ to declare the id; @id/ is for referencing an already-declared id.

content.question: Which Kotlin statement example matches what the instructor typed to introduce a button into Kotlin?
content.explanation: The Kotlin pattern is to declare a variable of the Button type and assign it with findViewById(R.id.<id>).

content.question: If you rename an id in XML to 'login_my_button', what else must you update?

options.text: Update all code references that use R.id.login_button to the new name

content.explanation: Renaming an id requires updating any code that references the old R.id.<name> identifier.

content.question: What does the .kt file suffix represent?
content.explanation: The .kt extension denotes a Kotlin source file.

content.question: Which Android component manages UI and user interaction as shown in the episode?
content.explanation: An Activity is the controller for the UI and handles user interactions.

content.question: When you create an activity and select 'Generate layout file', which naming convention did the instructor show for the layout?
content.explanation: The example showed a generated name like ActivityMyAndroid for the layout when creating the activity.
hints: The dialog shows the layout name field

content.question: In the instructor's example, what two files are typically generated when creating a new activity with layout?

options.text: An activity Kotlin/Java file and a layout XML file
A service and a broadcast receiver

content.explanation: Creating a new activity generates the controller (Kotlin/Java) and the UI layout XML when the option is enabled.

content.question: Which IDE file extension shows a Kotlin activity in the project tree?
content.explanation: Kotlin files appear with the .kt extension in the project tree.

content.question: During the demo the instructor restarted the emulator because the install was taking longer — why might you restart the emulator?

options.text: To resolve slow installs or stuck emulator state
To change the app package name

content.explanation: Restarting the emulator can help when installations hang or the device becomes unresponsive.
hints: Emulator restarts fix many device-side issues

content.question: Which view binding pattern did the instructor use manually in Kotlin in the episode?
content.explanation: He demonstrated introducing the component into Kotlin using findViewById with an explicit Button type.

content.question: What import did the IDE prompt for when declaring a Button variable in Kotlin?
content.explanation: The Button class comes from android.widget.Button and must be imported when referenced by type.

content.question: Which resource object holds generated ids like login_button?
content.explanation: IDs declared in XML are generated into the R.id class and referenced as R.id.<name>.

content.question: When the instructor searched for a color name and saw '1 out of 6', what does that number indicate?

options.text: The current match index and total matches (1 of 6 occurrences)

content.explanation: Find shows the current match position and the total number of matches found on the screen or scope.
hints: It helps you step through each occurrence

content.question: How do you reference a drawable resource named 'button_design' in layout XML?
content.explanation: Set android:background to @drawable/<name> to apply a drawable as the view background.

content.question: Which element inside a shape drawable did the instructor use for fill color?
content.explanation: The <solid> tag provides a uniform fill color for a shape drawable.

content.question: Which element controls rounded corners inside a shape drawable?
content.explanation: The <corners> element contains attributes like 'radius' or per-corner attributes to control rounded corners.
hints: radius inside <corners> applies to all corners

content.question: In the transcript the instructor typed '30 dB' when setting a radius — which Android unit was intended?
content.explanation: The transcript's 'dB' was a typo; the intended unit for layout dimensions is 'dp'.

content.question: What small stroke width did the instructor choose to make the outline visible but subtle?
content.explanation: He reduced the stroke width to 1dp for a fine, subtle outline.

content.question: How did the instructor demonstrate selecting multiple UI elements to change color across them?

options.text: Use Find and Replace to replace the color name across occurrences
Select each widget separately and change

content.explanation: He used the editor's find/replace to change the color name across multiple occurrences in one action.
hints: Find shows total matches like '1 out of 6'

content.question: What is the recommended place to design component-specific XML (like a button background) rather than using image assets?

options.text: Create a drawable resource file in res/drawable
Use layout XML for drawable definitions

content.explanation: For component backgrounds, create drawable XML files in res/drawable rather than using image or vector assets.
hints: Drawable XML is scalable and customizable

content.question: Which of these is NOT a correct way to reference a declared id in code?
content.explanation: '@+id/..' is an XML syntax and cannot be used directly in Kotlin code; code uses R.id.<name>.
hints: XML and code reference formats differ

content.question: What must you do in Kotlin to respond to a button click as the instructor intended?

options.text: Attach a click listener (setOnClickListener) to the button variable
Declare a new XML attribute for clicks

content.explanation: To make the button perform actions, add a click listener in the Kotlin controller, e.g., loginButton.setOnClickListener { ... }.

content.question: Which XML file must be edited to change the app's launcher activity or intent-filter?
content.explanation: Intent filters and launcher activity declarations are managed in AndroidManifest.xml.

content.question: The instructor emphasized knowing a component before operating on it; which sequence best matches his analogy?

options.text: Introduce/identify the component in code, then perform actions on it
Perform actions first and introduce later

content.explanation: He compared it to knowing your friend before sharing chocolate — you must introduce (find) the component in code before manipulating it.
hints: findViewById introduces the component into code
